title: Research record
description: One line of kb/research.jsonl. What was searched, what was found, and how far it was verified. Skills cite these by id (X-...) with a verbatim quote from `snippet` or `read`.

lens.description: which research agent / angle produced it

topic.description: the PASS/TARGET item or gap this informs; cite kb ids in `informs`

snippet.description: verbatim text from the search result

read.description: verbatim excerpt if the page could be fetched; null if fetch was blocked or never attempted

fetch_tool.description: how the text in read/snippet was obtained; record it whenever status is fetched. http is a plain GET returning the page's own bytes, so a snippet taken from it is genuinely verbatim. webfetch passes the page through a summariser that can introduce artifacts - fabricated backticks, invented list numbering, altered quote marks - so a snippet from it is a rendering of the page rather than the page itself. These are different grades of evidence and status:fetched alone does not distinguish them. Absent on records written before 2026-09-09, where the mechanism was never captured and cannot be recovered; verify those against the live page with tools/verify_snippets.py rather than guessing.

status.description: search-only: title/snippet from a search result, no direct fetch attempted; fetched: page content was read; blocked: a direct fetch was attempted and the egress proxy refused it (see egress_ref) -- the claim then rests on the search-result snippet, not on a live read

claim.description: what this record supports, in one sentence

egress_ref.description: id of the matching kb/egress-log.jsonl decision (G-nnnnn) for this record's access attempt; required in practice when status is fetched or blocked, since those are the two statuses that name a real proxy decision

verification.description: Written ONLY by tools/stamp_verification.py from a real fetch of `url` through the same path the gate uses (plain GET + capture.html_to_text). Never hand-written. A citation is valid only if its quote lives in a field this stamp marks verbatim, so an invented `read` cannot launder an invented quote: read_verbatim false makes every quote drawn from `read` fail.

method.description: the gate's own fetch+strip path; there is deliberately only one

page_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the stripped page text, so a page that changes under us shows as needing re-verification instead of rotting silently

snippet_verbatim.description: the record's snippet is a contiguous substring of the stripped page

read_verbatim.description: same for `read`; null when the record has no read field

unreachable.description: the page could not be retrieved at all. NOT evidence the record is wrong -- it means nothing is proven either way.

reason.description: why it is unreachable, e.g. 'HTTP 403' or 'arXiv API returns abstract only, PDF body unreachable'

verified_quotes.description: SHA-256 of each whitespace-normalised quote that a card profile draws from this record AND that was found verbatim on the page. Quote-level rather than field-level on purpose: a long `read` excerpt can drift on one formatting artifact while the sentence actually quoted is genuinely on the page, so a field-level verdict rejects honest citations and accepts nothing extra.
